summary: The article provides largely accurate information regarding DTAA benefits and the application process for a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) using Form 42 in India, though some references to the Income-tax Act of 1961 are outdated as it has been replaced by the Income-tax Act, 2025.

claims.claim: Form 42 is the prescribed online application form for Indian residents to request a TRC from the Income Tax Department.
claims.note: Form 42 is indeed the application form for TRC for Indian residents.

claims.claim: The legal framework for issuing TRCs is established under the Income-tax Act, 1961, and relevant rules.
claims.note: The Income-tax Act, 1961 was repealed and replaced by the Income-tax Act, 2025, effective April 1, 2026. The legal framework for TRCs is now under the Income-tax Act, 2025, and Rule 75(3) of the Income-tax Rules, 2026.

claims.claim: India has DTAAs with over 90 countries, including major economies like the USA, UK, UAE, Singapore, and Australia.
claims.note: India has DTAAs with over 94 countries as of 2025, and over 85 countries under Section 90 of the Income Tax Act, 1961.

claims.claim: The tax paid in the source country can be claimed as a credit against the tax payable in the country of residence. This credit is claimed when filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) in India, typically using Form 67.
claims.note: Form 67 is used to claim foreign tax credit in India.

claims.claim: A TRC is generally issued for a specific financial year. If you continue to earn foreign income in subsequent years, you will need to apply for a fresh TRC for each relevant financial year.
claims.note: A TRC is valid for one financial year and needs to be renewed annually.

claims.claim: The processing time for a TRC can vary, but generally, it is issued within a few weeks of a complete and correct application.
claims.note: The processing time for a TRC is typically a few weeks, with some sources suggesting 30-45 days or 6-8 weeks.

claims.claim: NRIs are not tax residents of India, so they cannot apply for an Indian TRC. They would need a TRC from their country of residence if they wish to claim DTAA benefits there.
claims.note: NRIs are not tax residents of India and therefore cannot apply for an Indian TRC. They obtain a TRC from their country of residence.

article_title: Claim DTAA Benefits: How to Apply for Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) using Form 42
